title: ESDM Auctions 14 Geothermal Blocks; Danantara Accounts Still Dark; EU Battery Storage Hits 36 GWh
dek: Indonesia's geothermal push accelerates into concrete procurement while the sovereign fund overseeing its SOE restructuring still cannot produce audited accounts — two structural conditions, not headlines.
summary: The Indonesian Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources has opened bidding on 14 new geothermal working areas, giving concrete form to Minister Bahlil's earlier ultimatum to concession-holders and marking the most significant auction cycle in the sector in years. Simultaneously, Danantara's financial statements remain unpublished months after inception, a governance gap that economists are now publicly flagging and that directly undermines the credibility of its BUMN Karya restructuring timeline — which management has set at end-2026. On the SOE side, Telkom has been directed by Danantara leadership to cut its subsidiary count to 18, a rare instance of the holding company exerting operational control rather than merely capital oversight. In European energy markets, battery storage installations reached 36 GWh in 2025, a 48% year-on-year increase that is reshaping the economics of variable renewable integration and creating a policy and procurement model worth tracking for Indonesia's own grid buildout. OpenAI's simultaneous launch of Zero Data Retention for API customers and a Private Safety Processing preview signals that enterprise AI adoption is entering a compliance-driven phase where data sovereignty, not raw capability, is the gating factor for regulated-sector deployment.

signals.headline: ESDM opens bidding on 14 new geothermal working areas, converting Bahlil's ultimatum into live procurement
signals.whatChanged: The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (Kementerian ESDM) has launched a tender for 14 new geothermal working areas (WKP). This follows Minister Bahlil's public rebuke of developers who have been sitting on concessions without progressing development, and comes against a backdrop of an Rp 2.6 trillion non-tax revenue (PNBP) target for the sector.
signals.whyItMatters: This continues the indonesia-geothermal-concession-reform thread. The shift from ministerial rhetoric to active procurement is the inflection point: 14 WKP on offer simultaneously represents a structural acceleration, not an incremental one. Indonesia holds the world's largest geothermal potential, and this auction cycle, if it attracts serious bids, will determine whether that potential is monetised in this decade or the next. The accumulation — ultimatum, then auction — now implies the government is prepared to use competitive pressure to break the concession-hoarding dynamic.
signals.secondOrder: A 14-block simultaneous auction creates a bidder-selection problem: the pool of technically and financially qualified geothermal developers globally is shallow. If bids cluster among two or three dominant players, the government risks recreating the concentration problem it is trying to solve. Conversely, if the auction attracts thin participation, it will expose the limits of coercive concession policy without complementary incentive reform — and will hand ammunition to those arguing the PNBP target is aspirational.
signals.action: Map the likely bidder universe against the 14 WKP by geography and resource quality this week. Identify which blocks are likely to attract multiple qualified bids versus which will require sweeteners (feed-in tariff, royalty holiday) to clear. That distinction will determine whether the auction is transformative or merely procedural.

signals.headline: Danantara financial statements still unpublished; economists flag governance risk as BUMN Karya deadline looms
signals.whatChanged: Danantara's financial statements have not been released, a fact that economists are now publicly criticising. This is happening concurrently with Danantara management reaffirming a year-end 2026 target for BUMN Karya restructuring completion and the IDX extending the trading suspension on WIKA shares.
signals.whyItMatters: This continues the danantara-bumn-karya-restructuring thread. The accumulation of signals — acknowledged structural barriers, 'phantom profit' concerns, a year-end deadline, and now an absent audit — means this is no longer a process-management challenge. It is a credibility challenge. A sovereign holding company that cannot produce timely financial statements cannot credibly represent to creditors, foreign partners, or the market that the restructuring values it is working with are real. The WIKA suspension extension is the market's answer to that question.
signals.secondOrder: The absence of published accounts creates a vacuum that will be filled by rumour and analyst inference, raising the cost of any capital Danantara or the BUMN Karya entities need to raise before year-end. More structurally, if the restructuring closes at end-2026 without audited baseline financials, the transaction prices will be contestable after the fact — creating litigation and renegotiation risk that could unwind agreed terms. The 'laba semu' (phantom profit) issue flagged in prior reporting becomes legally consequential, not merely reputational, in that scenario.
signals.action: Assess counterparty exposure to BUMN Karya entities — particularly WIKA and peers with suspended or illiquid shares — against the assumption that any restructuring valuation agreed before audited Danantara accounts are published carries a contingent restatement risk. Adjust contract and partnership terms with these entities accordingly.

signals.headline: Europe installs 36 GWh of battery storage in 2025, up 48% YoY; Ukraine enters top-five markets
signals.whatChanged: Europe added 36 GWh of new battery energy storage capacity in 2025, a 48% increase year-on-year, according to SolarPower Europe. Germany remained the largest market. Ukraine entered the top five — an unexpected entrant given the conflict context, likely driven by grid resilience imperatives.
signals.whyItMatters: The 48% growth rate sustained at 36 GWh scale means battery storage in Europe has crossed from early-adopter to mainstream infrastructure procurement. At this trajectory, storage is no longer a hedge against variable renewable output — it is a foundational grid asset that changes the economics of peaking capacity, ancillary services markets, and fossil backup. The Ukraine data point is particularly significant: it demonstrates that storage deployment can accelerate under extreme grid stress, which has implications for other markets facing reliability challenges.
signals.secondOrder: As European storage volumes scale, the procurement leverage of European utilities and grid operators over battery manufacturers will increase, driving cost curves down faster than IEA central scenarios anticipate. This benefits markets like Indonesia that are later movers — but only if Indonesian policy frameworks (grid codes, storage tariff structures, ancillary services markets) are ready to absorb the technology when it arrives at competitive cost. Currently they are not, which means the cost advantage will be partially offset by regulatory friction.
signals.action: Use the SolarPower Europe 36 GWh data point to benchmark Indonesia's own storage pipeline against a market that has achieved scale. Identify the specific regulatory instruments — grid code amendments, ancillary services market rules, storage-specific licensing — that Indonesia would need to activate to capture the cost reduction wave expected in 2027-2028 as European procurement volumes drive further price compression.

signals.headline: OpenAI formalises Zero Data Retention for frontier models and previews Private Safety Processing for enterprise API customers
signals.whatChanged: OpenAI has formally reaffirmed Zero Data Retention (ZDR) availability for eligible API customers across its frontier models and announced a preview of Private Safety Processing — a mechanism designed to run safety checks without OpenAI accessing the underlying prompt content. Both are positioned at enterprise and regulated-sector buyers.
signals.whyItMatters: Enterprise AI adoption in regulated sectors — financial services, healthcare, government — has been gated not by capability but by data residency and processing transparency requirements. ZDR removes the data retention objection; Private Safety Processing addresses the deeper concern that safety infrastructure itself creates a data exposure vector. Together, these lower the compliance barrier for regulated-sector deployment more than any model capability improvement has done in the past 12 months.
signals.secondOrder: If data sovereignty guarantees become a standard competitive feature rather than a premium differentiator, the basis of competition in enterprise AI shifts toward integration depth, workflow specificity, and SLA reliability — areas where incumbents with existing enterprise relationships (Microsoft via Azure OpenAI, Google via Workspace) have structural advantages over direct OpenAI API access. Paradoxically, OpenAI's compliance improvements may accelerate adoption primarily through its cloud partners rather than through its own direct channels.
signals.action: Review any enterprise AI procurement framework or vendor evaluation currently in progress: update the data governance evaluation criteria to include Private Safety Processing architecture, not just contractual ZDR commitments. Ask vendors to demonstrate how safety processing is isolated from training pipelines — the architecture, not just the policy, is what matters for regulatory sign-off.

signals.headline: Danantara directs Telkom to cut subsidiaries to 18, marking first visible operational intervention by the holding
signals.whatChanged: Danantara leadership has called in Telkom management and directed the company to reduce its number of subsidiaries to 18. This is a concrete, named operational instruction — not a strategic aspiration — and represents the first clearly documented instance of Danantara exercising active portfolio management over an SOE rather than functioning purely as a passive capital vehicle.
signals.whyItMatters: The governance architecture of Danantara has been debated since inception: is it a holding company with real operational authority, or a financial wrapper? This instruction to Telkom answers that question in the affirmative for at least one large SOE. The subsidiary rationalisation model — if applied consistently — implies significant disposals, workforce restructuring, and inter-subsidiary contract renegotiation across Telkom's ecosystem, which extends into digital infrastructure, financial services, and cloud.
signals.secondOrder: Telkom's subsidiary network includes companies with significant third-party commercial relationships and minority investors. Forced consolidation to 18 entities will trigger change-of-control clauses, minority buyout obligations, and potential regulatory notifications in sectors where subsidiary-level licensing applies (e.g. telecommunications spectrum, financial services). The speed of execution Danantara demands will determine whether these obligations are managed or contested.
signals.action: Identify which of Telkom's current subsidiaries fall outside the implied 18-entity perimeter and carry third-party minority stakes, licensed spectrum, or material customer contracts. Those are the units most likely to require structured divestiture processes rather than simple wind-downs — and the ones where transaction advisors will be needed in Q4 2026.

watchNext.item: Geothermal WKP auction bid submission deadlines and qualified bidder list — will participation be deep enough to validate the 14-block simultaneous strategy?
Danantara first audited financial statement publication — absence beyond Q3 2026 would make any BUMN Karya restructuring valuation formally contestable.
Telkom subsidiary disposal announcements — which of the entities outside the 18-unit perimeter attract third-party bidders versus internal consolidation?
SolarPower Europe mid-year 2026 storage update — whether the 48% growth rate is sustained or decelerating, and which new markets enter the top five.
OpenAI Private Safety Processing general availability and first regulated-sector (financial or government) deployment announcements.
